name: What type of pool finish works best with salt water?

mainEntity.name: Should a new saltwater pool use plaster, pebble, quartz, or another finish in Southern California?
mainEntity.text: Should a new saltwater pool use plaster, pebble, quartz, or another finish in Southern California?

acceptedAnswer.text: The best finish for a saltwater pool depends on budget, comfort, durability, and how much maintenance the owner is willing to do. Basic plaster is usually the lowest-cost option, but it may show wear sooner if water balance is not maintained. Quartz and pebble finishes generally offer better durability and can be a smart choice for saltwater pools that will see frequent use. The finish also affects feel, appearance, and how visibly salt residue or scaling may show. In a warm climate like Los Angeles, where pools get heavy sun exposure and frequent use, owners often prefer finishes that are easier to keep looking uniform over time. The most important factor is not just the finish itself but whether the pool is kept in proper balance during startup and operation. Ask the builder which finishes they recommend for saltwater use, how each affects warranty, and what maintenance is needed for the first year. A good finish choice can reduce future repairs and staining.
acceptedAnswer.description: Saltwater pools can use several finishes, but durability and maintenance vary. Quartz and high-quality pebble finishes often hold up better than basic plaster, especially when the pool is heavily used or the water chemistry drifts. The best choice depends on budget, texture preference, and how much maintenance the owner wants to handle.
